html:
SMTO-DB-0018 — SMTO couldn't finish finding your databases

GUID: 4dff9081-d6ad-4c52-bb82-64e7fe17e36b
Slug: database-discovery-failed
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • SMTO tried to list the databases on your PostgreSQL database server but stopped without a usable list. Nothing was added to or changed in Parameter Store.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the database details you entered: server name, port, username and password. Make sure the database server is switched on and reachable from the computer running your Gateway. SMTO lists databases by connecting from the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run work on a computer), so a wrong detail or an unreachable server leaves nothing to list.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on the Gateway you use. The database search runs on that Gateway, so it must be connected for the search to work.
  3. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu (the ⋯ button at the top) and make sure your saved entries load, and note which databases are already listed there. Found databases are saved into Parameter Store, so it must be working, and checking first avoids saving duplicates.
  4. Run the database search again the same way you started it, and save from the new list, not from an older one. An older list may no longer match Parameter Store if someone changed entries since it was made.

What success looks like

  • The search shows a list of your databases, and the ones you save appear in Parameter Store.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO and your database server. Don't paste the database password into a chat or email when you ask for help.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Database discovery returned status error with empty discovered, created and updated lists and a redacted diagnostic, under a failure code that has no more specific catalog entry.

What this means

  • The discovery error wrapper receives a failure code/message and emits empty discovered/created/updated lists with a bounded diagnostic. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • The discovery error wrapper receives a failure code/message and emits empty discovered/created/updated lists with a bounded diagnostic.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific discovery code and cause; the wrapper alone cannot distinguish connection, execution or parsing failure.

How to fix it

  • Read the error code and redacted diagnostic in errors[0] and error_detail of the /api/agent/databases/discover (or /discover/commit) response. Verify engine, host, port, user, password and sslmode, confirm the selected Gateway can reach the PostgreSQL host with psql, and confirm Parameter Store is available before committing; then run discovery again to get fresh drafts instead of committing stale ones.
  • Inspect the bounded diagnostic and the discovery connection configuration before another read.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The cause is established and a supported discovery read returns a valid listing.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
